newsitem.title: USA: U.S. refiners show weak appetite for foreign crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. refiners show weak appetite for foreign crude.

text.p: U.S. refiners showed a weak appetite for foreign crude Thursday despite a plethora of offers, traders said.
Three VLCC's of North Sea Brent crude are on their way across the Atlantic to the U.S. Gulf Coast, and should arrive around mid- to late January, traders said.
The sellers, which include at least two Wall Street players, are asking for a discount of 20 cents to February West Texas Intermediate.
"There is foreign crude available, but it is a fact that we don't need it. The margins are so poor," a trader for a major U.S. refiner said.
The spread between February WTI and North Sea Brent was around $1.60 a barrel.
Short-haul barrels from Latin America are also arousing only moderate interest, traders said.
British Petroleum is offering sweet Colombian Cusiana crude for the end of January at March WTI plus 10 cents.
Shell Oil is offering Colombian Vasconia loading January 20-21 at March WTI minus $1.85.

Meanwhile, Colombia's state-owned Ecopetrol failed to receive any acceptable offers for a cargo of 550,000 barrels of Cano Limon for February 10-15 in a tender earlier this week. The firm was asking March WTI minus minus $1.20-30 a barrel, traders said.
In the U.S. aftermarket, a partial paper Brent cargo changed hands at $24.30 a barrel, up six cents from the IPE settlement.
A full boat of paper March Brent was traded at $23.75, up 17 cents from the London close. Partials traded at $23.70/23.72/23.73 a barrel.
Intermonth spreads were weaker. Feb/Mar Brent traded at 60/62 cents, down four to six cents from the London settlement.
